Consult Summary:
- Patient reports 2 months of escalating work-related anxiety with significant sleep disturbance, low mood, and morning palpitations since starting a new job.
- Agreed plan for self-referral to NHS talking therapy (CBT), use of online resources, sleep hygiene advice, basic blood tests, and GP follow-up after results.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Work-related anxiety with low mood and functional impact (onset ~2 months, coinciding with starting new retail head office job; boss interactions stressful).
- Symptoms: daily dread of work; persistent worry; low energy; anhedonia; decreased socializing; reduced exercise (less running/tennis); appetite largely unchanged but increased chocolate intake; no prior similar severe episode.
- Sleep: difficulty initiating and maintaining sleep; total ~3–4 hours/night; wakes early with racing heart (see Issue 2).
- Mood: feels “down” most days including weekends; denies suicidal ideation; has good family support.
- Social: lives with parents.
- Management: patient agreeable to one-to-one therapy; advised self-referral to NHS talking therapies; online resources suggested; safety-net to call back if worsening or unable to cope; medication may be considered if non-response to therapy (not first-line).

Issue 2:
- Palpitations likely anxiety-related.
- Features: mainly on waking/mornings when worried about being late; described as “irregular”; lasts minutes up to ~10 minutes; no chest pain initially, later stated it is “painful when heart is beating fast” (conflict noted); new over past ~2 months.
- Plan: basic blood tests to exclude medical triggers; arrange GP follow-up 1 week after tests to review results.

Issue 3:
- Insomnia related to anxiety.
- Features: bedtime 10–11 pm; prolonged sleep latency (lying awake for hours); early awakening before alarm with palpitations; reports shallow sleep; estimated 3–4 hours/night.
- Plan: sleep hygiene advice to be provided in notes; use of online self-help resources.

Medications:
- No regular medications documented.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Lives with parents.
- Employment: new role in fashion retailer head office; high stress since starting ~2 months ago.
- Alcohol: “quite a lot” on Fri/Sat (likely over weekly limit on those days) plus occasional glass of wine during the week; does not routinely track intake.
- Smoking: occasional; tries not to smoke.
- Recreational drugs: denies.

Preventative History:
- Not documented (cervical screening, mammogram, prostate test, fecal occult blood test, bone density, vaccinations, optometry/skin check not discussed).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination: not documented (remote consultation).

Plan:
- Provide link for self-referral to NHS talking therapies (CBT).
- Provide online mental health resources and sleep hygiene information.
- Arrange basic blood tests (patient to call support line to book).
- Schedule GP follow-up 1 week after blood tests to discuss results.
- Safety net: patient to call back if symptoms worsen, if unable to cope with work/daily activities, or if current measures are not helping.
- Discussed that medication may be considered if therapy/other measures are insufficient (not initiated today).

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: current medication list and reconciliation; drug allergies; vitals/exam; formal screening scores (GAD-7/PHQ-9); detailed suicide/self-harm risk assessment; specific labs to be ordered not specified.
- Internal conflicts: patient initially denied chest pain but later described pain when heart beats fast during palpitations (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: generally clear with minor inaudible/fragmented segments; sufficient for clinical documentation.
